graph_route.verdict: One candidate remains: same pinned Cargo 1.97.1 (c980f4866141969fab6254a680546a277789d6f0) planner behind an explicit, narrowly confined development-channel gate. Not approved. candidates.name: Same pinned Cargo, development-channel gate
candidates.planner_identity: Same code path by construction: create_bcx runs for both graph and ordinary build; the only divergence is the emit at cargo_compile/mod.rs:188-190 and the nightly_features_allowed branches listed below.

gate.channel_env: __CARGO_TEST_CHANNEL_OVERRIDE_DO_NOT_USE_THIS=nightly (preferred). Read only by Cargo (features.rs:1563-1566). Test-only, undocumented, unvalidated value.
gate.rejected_channel_env: RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1 maps the Cargo channel to dev (features.rs:1570-1573) but is also read by rustc itself, enabling unstable rustc features in every probe and child rustc. Not acceptable as the gate.
gate.cli: cargo build|test --unit-graph -Z unstable-options --frozen (+ the identical ordinary argv). --unit-graph exists on build (commands/build.rs:38) and test (commands/test.rs:60) and is gated by fail_if_stable_opt (command_prelude.rs:823-825).
gate.fail_closed: If the override or the flag is removed upstream, the graph run fails with Cargo's own 'only available on the nightly channel' refusal (features.rs:1476-1505). It cannot silently succeed on stable.

context/mod.rs:1155 -Z flag parse (CliUnstable::parse call gated by nightly_features_allowed).
context/mod.rs:1226 [unstable] config table loaded only when nightly_features_allowed.
features.rs:1244-1246 any -Z flag refused when not nightly.
features.rs:681-684 manifest cargo-features with Status::Unstable accepted only when nightly_features_allowed (manifest-level divergence from ordinary stable).
features.rs:439,610,625,764 feature-set plumbing and diagnostics text.

candidates.inventory_caveat: Built from the 14 fetched files only. A complete grep of nightly_features_allowed and channel() across the whole pinned tree is a precondition of any implementation brief; it was not performed here.

sites: target_info.rs:168-221 TargetInfo::new runs rustc --print=file-names/sysroot/split-debuginfo/crate-name/cfg per requested kind (RustcTargetData::new at cargo_compile/mod.rs:285 precedes units).
util/rustc.rs:65-68 rustc -vV through the cached Rustc::new path; cache file at ws.build_dir()/.rustc_info.json (context/mod.rs:510-511).
cargo_compile/mod.rs:222 print path (not used by the graph route).
rustc_probes.consequence: Graph construction always executes the consumer's rustc (or build.rustc / RUSTC wrapper) and writes the rustc-info cache under the build directory. Both must be private and receipted. Probes count as children of the Cargo invocation.

config_reach.apply_env_config: core/compiler/mod.rs:2643-2655 applies every [env] table value to rustc/probe ProcessBuilders unless Cargo itself already set that key on that builder. Inherited process env is not checked. So a config [env] RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP or override key reaches rustc in ordinary runs (target_info.rs:188, 325; util/rustc.rs:65).
config_reach.channel_not_config: channel() reads the process env at startup only, so [env] cannot flip the Cargo gate itself.
config_reach.consumer_rule: Refuse any [env] entry, --config env.* value, build.rustc*/RUSTC* wrapper, or [unstable] table in both graph and ordinary runs. The empty allow-list is simpler than a denylist.

side_effects_and_lock.lock: ops/lockfile.rs:55-66 refuses lock writes when locked_flag is set; locked_flag returns --frozen before --locked (context/mod.rs:1272-1280). Use --frozen: it also sets offline_flag (context/mod.rs:1254-1262) and blocks network_allowed (context/mod.rs:1250-1252).
side_effects_and_lock.network_enforcement_gap: The source-layer point where network_allowed is enforced for index/git/crate downloads was not in the fetched set (package.rs download_accessible at :619-627 does not show it). Treat --frozen as necessary but unverified by source; prefer a private directory-vendored source so no network source exists.
side_effects_and_lock.writes: Rustc-info cache under build dir; package cache under CARGO_HOME (private); no target artifacts, because compile_ws returns before BuildRunner (cargo_compile/mod.rs:188-191 per 041).

candidates.behaviour_gap: Manifest cargo-features and -Z/[unstable] accepted only under the gate. A graph success therefore does not imply ordinary stable success. The consumer must refuse any manifest cargo-features key, any [unstable] table, and any -Z in argv/config before the graph run, and must refuse graph output containing public/noprelude/nounused.

binding_contract_proposed.invocation_equivalence: The graph invocation argv must equal the ordinary argv plus exactly {--unit-graph, -Z, unstable-options, --frozen}; the env must equal the ordinary env plus exactly {__CARGO_TEST_CHANNEL_OVERRIDE_DO_NOT_USE_THIS=nightly}. Any other difference refuses. The ordinary build/test must then use the same subcommand as the graph (build graph does not bind test units).
provenance_record_fields: Cargo binary identity from the installed-tool receipt, plus version string and pinned commit
rustc -vV digest, host triple, and build.rustc/RUSTC resolved path identity
exact source tree identity of the selected commit (Git tree), not a per-file digest
Cargo.lock digest before and after (must be equal, and the graph must have run --frozen)
manifest set digest and effective-config inventory digest (file set, not secret values)
env snapshot digest with secrets removed, plus CARGO_HOME, CARGO_TARGET_DIR and build-dir identity
graph bytes digest, schema version, and clock/invocation accounting
binding_contract_proposed.unit_binding: Decoder accepts only version=1 and refuses unknown fields. Each unit's target src_path must lie under a registered consumer root or refuse. The graph root set must equal the ordinary argv's root selection. Binding is to units for one argv; a changed selector, profile, feature, target or command needs a new graph.
binding_contract_proposed.authority: The provenance record is produced by the consumer's admitted host run and settled by the consumer owner. Oxide verifies bytes and binding. No issuer attestation is created by this design.

refusal_rules: Unsupported Cargo version/commit, or override env name absent at the pin: refuse.
Any [env], --config env.*, RUSTC*/build.rustc* wrapper, [unstable] table, -Z outside the gate, or manifest cargo-features: refuse both graph and ordinary runs.
Lock digest changes or lock missing under --frozen: refuse.
Graph JSON with unknown version, unknown field, public/noprelude/nounused, or absolute path outside registered roots: refuse.
Any probe, wrapper or child not inside the receipted tool set: refuse.

installation_evidence.verdict: Recommend owner-installed immutable receipts (C) with bounded streaming complete-content verification (B). Reject a per-file cap raise as the default route (A). Budgets below are PROPOSALS, unmeasured and unruled.

facts_used.cc: relative symlink to clang (5 bytes), resolves to clang
facts_used.in_repo_registered_rs: src/registered.rs:62-74 Limits::NUCLEUS; ImmutableClass {Registry, ToolSdk} at :229-232; file() stability check via ctime/stamp before and after read at :559-573; membership refuses symlinks and special entries at :638-690 and caps visits at associations.
facts_used.admission_read_budget: nucleus-core-reuse.md Finite read budgets: 520 MiB accepted reads for admission and independently for finalize (256 source inventory + 8 map + 256 collection).

options.name: Raise ToolSdk per-file cap
options.reason: Weakens the unchanged per-file bound for every ToolSdk user and keeps the complete-root membership requirement, which is the harder problem. Allowed only as a separately versioned, constructor-installed class if B is ruled out.

options.name: Bounded streaming complete-content verification
options.design: Hash each listed file in fixed 1 MiB chunks (resident memory = chunk + manifest). Per-file byte cap is a class-specific constructor parameter. Stat before and after; refuse when dev/inode/size/mtime/ctime changed (same pattern as registered.rs:559-573). No sampled digest, no split-file or chunk exemption, no size-only check.
options.cost: Read cost per phase = sum of closure bytes. Admission and finalize each hash the full closure again, so cargo+clang alone costs 2 x 149.28 MiB = 298.56 MiB of reads per run before any SDK bytes. No copy: verify and execute in place, so no write amplification. Hash throughput is unmeasured; no time claim.

options.name: Owner-installed immutable receipt with no-replacement epoch
options.design: The installation owner commits a manifest: root identity, epoch id, per-entry {relative path, kind, size, mode (metadata only), sha256 or exact link target, device/inode}, the declared required closure, and an installer statement of the epoch's no-replacement promise. Consumer owner accepts it under its acceptance conditions. Oxide verifies the bytes against it (B). Any mismatch refuses and marks the epoch invalid; no auto re-accept. A new toolchain or Xcode update creates a new epoch needing fresh acceptance.
options.trust_boundary: Detection, not prevention. rustup and Xcode roots are user-writable, so OS immutability is not assumed. Residual risk: same-UID replacement between the last identity check and exec. This is the cooperative same-UID model already recorded in nucleus-core-reuse.md. The receipt is an accepted commitment, not a signature; no signing issuer is created.

options.name: Narrowed root with complete membership
options.verdict: Allowed only as a receipt over an explicitly named root with a declared required closure
options.reason: Partial closure with no declared root boundary is refused. A narrowed root must list every entry under that root and state why the rest cannot affect the build (sysroot/rustlib and SDK closure must be included). The sizes of those roots are unmeasured.

proposed_budgets_unruled.class_name_proposed: InstalledToolReceipt (constructor-installed, versioned; not an existing class)
proposed_budgets_unruled.per_file_note: Covers cargo (30.39 MiB) and clang (118.90 MiB) with headroom; applies only to this class. The 16 MiB source/archive/member policy and Limits::NUCLEUS are unchanged.
proposed_budgets_unruled.per_phase_aggregate_bytes: 1 GiB proposed, to be fixed only after a measured closure inventory
proposed_budgets_unruled.admission_accepted_reads: 520 MiB existing plus a separate tool-receipt term. The existing 520 MiB already fills source inventory, map and collection, so receipt reads cannot fit inside it. Owner ruling required, applied independently at finalize.
proposed_budgets_unruled.metadata_budget: one lstat per entry visited plus one stat before and after each regular-file read, all counted against visits <= root_membership_entries
proposed_budgets_unruled.write_budget: 0 in the proposal (verify in place). Any private copy must add an explicit write budget.

installation_evidence.symlink_rule: Record a link as an entry with its exact target string. Refuse absolute links, links that leave the receipted root, dangling links, hardlinks (shared inode without both listed), and special files. A link is covered by its target's single hash; its bytes are not counted twice. cc -> clang is one clang read.
installation_evidence.unverified_041_claim: 041 wrote that rustup and Xcode roots contain 'far more than 32768 entries'. That was not enumerated in 041 or 042. It stays unverified until a scoped inventory.
owner_commitments_needed: Rust toolchain owner: installed root identity, rustc -vV commit and host, cargo and rustc binary entries, sysroot/rustlib closure, epoch id and no-replacement promise.
Xcode/native owner: chosen clang/cc/ar/ld paths from observed PATH and xcrun, complete membership of the chosen root(s), SDK headers/frameworks subset actually required, epoch id and promise.
Consumer (Nucleus) owner: acceptance conditions for the class, the admission/finalize tool-read term, and the decision to refuse on unknown or uncommitted entries.
installation_evidence.refusal_and_unknown: Overflow, unreadable entry, changed identity, unknown epoch, unsupported link or any mismatch refuses before spawn. Unknown outcome retains bytes and holds ownership. Ordinary fresh private validation remains the fallback.

recommended_sequence.scope: Oxide-only library work with owned fixtures; no Cargo execution, no host reads
recommended_sequence.content: Unit-graph version=1 decoder and provenance binding verifier (argv/env/config/lock/source/tool digests; path-under-root; root-set equality). Fixtures hand-written from the pinned serializer shape.

recommended_sequence.scope: Oxide-only library work with owned fixtures
recommended_sequence.content: InstalledToolReceipt schema, streaming full-content verifier, symlink and membership rules, identity stability checks, constructor-installed per-class budgets. Bounded synthetic files only; no real tool content.

recommended_sequence.scope: Consumer owner (Nucleus) contract change; not an Oxide brief
recommended_sequence.content: Accept or decline the receipt class, the separate tool-read admission and finalize term, and epoch acceptance. Contract011/NucleusContract002 departure needs the owner's later agreement.

recommended_sequence.scope: Material ruling plus scoped host-read brief
recommended_sequence.content: One bounded inventory of the declared roots (counts, sizes, link targets, no hashing beyond the approved budget). First measurement that can settle fit.
Approve or refuse the development-channel gate (candidate A) with the exact env, flags, refusal set, nightly-branch inventory, and a changed trial cap if needed.
One real graph + receipt trial with fresh time, Cargo-count and resource caps. Not authorized here.

trial_accounting.graph_call: One cargo build|test --unit-graph invocation. It counts as one of the original 4 Cargo invocations and its full wall time, including rustc probes, resolution and any download attempt, counts against the 45-minute clock. No separate allowance.
trial_accounting.probes: Each rustc probe is a child of the graph invocation. It is not a separate Cargo invocation, but its count and time must be reported under that invocation.
trial_accounting.receipt_verification: Receipt hashing is outside Cargo but inside the attempt. A trial clock must cover it, or the trial silently excludes it. Proposed: the attempt clock includes it.
trial_accounting.consequence: A trial with a graph call leaves 3 Cargo invocations and the remaining minutes for build and test. Any changed cap is a separate material ruling.
trial_accounting.no_silent_preparation: No extra graph, probe or metadata call is allowed beyond those named in the executing brief.

maintenance_and_first_benefit.route_A_burden: Moderate. Pinned-version refusal, an unstable env that could be removed (fail-closed), a re-audit of nightly branches on each Cargo upgrade, and a decoder and binding layer.
maintenance_and_first_benefit.receipt_burden: Moderate to high. Epoch re-acceptance on every Rust or Xcode update; full re-hash of the closure on each admission and finalize.
maintenance_and_first_benefit.first_storage_benefit: The graph and receipts serve the stricter cross-root and unit-binding claim. They do not supply first storage relief. Same-root dependency reuse was shown by Task021 without a graph. First relief depends on the owner pool path and Cargo's own fingerprints. Recommendation: do not start the graph/receipt trial until the owner path and Tom's ruling make the stricter claim necessary.

owner_gates: Nucleus graph/audited-input owner: accept the graph provenance seam.
Nucleus task-admission and Queue host owners: accept the tool-receipt term in admission and finalize.
Tom: unstable channel gate ruling; any changed trial cap; any per-file or aggregate ceiling beyond the 16 MiB unchanged default.
Real-issuer, native/C closure, proc-macro helper closure and debug/capture gates remain open.

observed: Pinned Cargo channel override, RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP mapping, nightly_features_allowed reach, unit-graph gate, [env] apply reach, rustc probe and rustc-info cache sites, lock and offline helpers, unit graph v1 schema.
Oxide in-repo registered.rs Limits, ImmutableClass, stability check and membership refusals.
